programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.sub-title: Countryside and Creation at the Royal Norfolk Show
programme.desc: The Rev Kate Bottley visits the Royal Norfolk Show - one of the largest agricultural events in the country, and one that has been celebrating food and farming in the county for nearly 180 years. There, she meets Christians living out their faith in farming communities across the county. She meets the Bishop of Lynn, the Rt Rev Jane Steen, who explains why having a Christian presence at the show is important and the Rev Dr Tim Weatherstone who is taking on the role of rural chaplain in the county. Anna Mudeka, leader of the African Choir of Norfolk who are performing in the show's Carnival of Cultures, explains the importance of togetherness and talks about the choir's involvement at the archbishop of Canterbury's installation service

Alan believed he 'lost' 25 minutes, during which time he was on board the craft being medically examined by small beings and a tall man with a beard

programme.title: Craig Charles: UFO Conspiracies
programme.desc: In January 2008, a shadow was cast over the town of Stephenville, Texas, when a UFO passed overhead at supersonic speed. The event was witnessed by scores of stunned locals who remain desperate for answers on what exactly they saw that winter's evening. Craig and space journalist Sarah Cruddas talk to eyewitness private pilot Steve Allen who was with friends when he saw a vast UFO passing overhead at a speed estimated to be 2,000mph. He describes the craft as having an array of bright, high-intensity lights at its rear - and pursued by two US Air Force F16 fighter jets. The team discovers that the US military, who initially denied any knowledge of this event, changed their story in the weeks following the incident, adding fuel to the theory that there could be a high-level cover-up

programme.title: Craig Charles: UFO Conspiracies

programme.title: River Hunters
programme.desc: Rick Edwards and Beau Ouimette head to north Wales to investigate waterways that may contain signs of the medieval Welsh Rebellion. Conwy Castle was constructed by Edward I between 1283-1287 after the Welsh Rebellion of 1282-3. The castle was part of a chain of fortifications known as the 'Iron Ring of Castles' and was both a material and symbolic sign of English power and dominance. Edward I selected its site on a high rock perched above the estuary of the River Conwy so that the castle could be supplied by the river in times of siege. Day two finds the pair at Ruthin Castle, a medieval fortress overlooking the River Clwyd

programme.title: River Hunters

The fort occupied a key strategic route through Perthshire and into north-east Scotland from the First to Third centuries

programme.title: Cruising Paradise: Above and Below Deck
programme.desc: As the Star Princess approaches Belize, gusting 40-knot winds force commodore Nick Nash into an agonising call: abort the port and send thousands of disappointed guests back out to sea. It's the ship's first cancelled stop, and cruise director Dan and his team have just 20 minutes to create an entire replacement day of entertainment. And the ship's entertainment cast are gearing up for their final performance, as dancers Adam, Emma and Cassie reach the end of 10-month contracts that have made them a family thousands of miles from home. A new troupe, including Mia from Stoke and Zahra from Milton Keynes, are already rehearsing back on dry land, ready to step into their shoes. After a sunny stop on the Honduran island of Roatán, complete with a fun rope jump into water gone wrong, the outgoing cast take to the stage in the Arena theatre for the very last time, torn between excitement for whatever comes next and the sadness of saying goodbye to the people who've become their family at sea

programme.title: Lego Masters Australia
programme.desc: Hamish Blake hosts with judge Ryan 'Brickman' McNaught, as Lego Masters veterans from across Canada, China, Finland, Sweden, the USA and New Zealand face off against Australia's top homegrown talent in a global showdown of epic proportions. The ten teams of two - six international teams and four Aussie, and all former Lego Masters winners or finalists in their respective countries - will put their imaginations, creativity and building skills to the test. But only one pair can be crowned the champions and take home a galactical $100,000. In this first challenge, the veteran builders have 12 hours to construct a creative functioning section of a great ball contraption, all of which are linked in a circle. When the build time is up, a ball must transfer seamlessly from the tube on one team's table to the next, while passing through epic Lego designs that tell a story. The catch? If the ball doesn't pass through one team's build, they will score zero points

programme.desc: Coverage of the evening session on day six from Alexander Stadium in Birmingham. programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster explores the Galapagos, a collection of volcanic islands in the Pacific known for its extraordinary wildlife. More than 150 years after Charles Darwin formulated his ground-breaking theory of evolution on the remote archipelago, Attenborough explains how life on the islands has continued to evolve in biological isolation, examining how the ever-changing volcanic landscape has given birth to species and sub-species that exist nowhere else in the world. He begins by revealing how Galapagos rose from the ocean four million years ago

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos

programme.title: 1066: A Year to Conquer England
